title: Why planets keep orbiting
topic: Why do planets orbit the Sun?
summary: A planet moves forward while the Sun's gravity continually bends its path inward.

scenes.learningGoal: See that a moving planet would continue forward without gravity.
scenes.narration: Start with the planet moving sideways. If nothing changed its motion, it would continue along this straight dotted path.
scenes.caption: Motion continues in a straight line unless a force changes it.

scenes.learningGoal: Understand that gravity accelerates the planet toward the Sun.
scenes.narration: The Sun's gravity pulls the planet inward. That inward acceleration changes the direction of the planet's velocity at every moment.
scenes.caption: Gravity changes direction; it does not create an outward force.

scenes.learningGoal: Combine forward motion and inward acceleration into an orbit.
scenes.narration: Put the two ideas together. The planet keeps moving forward, while gravity continually turns its path inward. It keeps falling around the Sun instead of flying away or crashing straight in.
scenes.caption: An orbit is continuous free fall around the Sun.

quiz.question: What does gravity do to an orbiting planet?
quiz.explanation: Gravity accelerates the planet inward, continually changing the direction of its velocity.

quiz.question: Why does the planet not fall straight into the Sun?
quiz.explanation: Its forward velocity carries it sideways while gravity bends the path inward.
